FIXED AMOUNT OF CENTRAL EXCISE DUTY RULES, 1997
FIXED AMOUNT OF CENTRAL EXCISE DUTY RULES, 1997
[Gazette of Pakistan, Extraordinary, Part II,
24th November, 1997]
S.R.O. 1189(I)/97, dated, 24-11-1997.-----In exercise of the powers conferred by
subsections (8) and (9) of section 3 of the Central Excises Act, 1944 (I of
1944), read with section 37 thereof, the Central Board of Revenue, with the
prior approval of the Federal Government, is pleased to make the following
rules for the levy and collection of excise duty in lieu of central excise duty
leviable under subsection (1) of the said section, namely:--
1. Short title, application and commencement.-----(1) These rules may be called the Fixed Amount
of Central Excise Duty Rules, 1997.
(2) They shall apply to the manufacturers of goods specified in the
Schedule to these rules.
(3) They shall come into force at once and, unless repealed earlier,
shat remain in force during the financial year 1997-98.
2. Definitions.---(1)
In these rules, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,--
(a) "Act" means the Central Excises Act, 1944 (1 of 1944);
(b) "Assistant Collector" means the Assistant Collector of
Central Excise in whose jurisdiction the manufacturer's business is situated:
Provided that where there is no Assistant Collector, it shall mean the
Deputy Collector of Central Excise in whose jurisdiction, the manufacturer's
business is situated.
(c) "Association" means the respective association of the
manufacturers duly recognised by the Federal Government;
(d) "Board" means the Central Board of Revenue;
(e) "Collector" means the Collector of Central Excise in whose
jurisdiction the manufacturer's business is situated;
(f) "Joint Survey Committee" means the Joint Survey Committee
constituted under sub-rule (2) of rule 6;
(g) "manufacturer" means the manufacturer of goods specified
in the Schedule;
(h) "Schedule" means the Schedule to these rules; and
(i) "Superintendent" means the Superintendent of Central
Excise in whose jurisdiction the manufacturer's business is situated.
(2) All other expressions used, but not defined in these rules, shall
have the meaning assigned to them in the Act.
3. Guiding principles for fixation of duty.---(1) The fixed amount of duty payable by an
establishment or undertaking during the year 1997-98 shall be worked out by the
Collectors of Central Excise having the jurisdiction on the basis of the
following guiding principles, namely:--
(i) only such manufacturers will come under the fixed duty scheme who
have been paying fixed amount of excise duty during the years 1995-96 and
1996-97 and opt to pay fixed amount of excise duty for the year 1997-98 as
worked out under these rules;
(ii) financial year 1995-96 shall be taken as the base year for working
out the fixed amount of duty payable by an establishment or undertaking for the
financial year 1997-98;
(iii) fixed amount of duty for the financial year 1996-97 shall be
twenty per cent. more than the amount of duty fixed for the financial year
1995-96;
(iv) fixed amount of duty for the financial year 1997-98 shall be forty
per cent, more than the amount of duty fixed for the financial year 1996-97 in
terms of clause (iii)-or sixty-eight per cent. more than the amount of duty
fixed for the year 1995-96 whichever is higher; and
(v) fixed amount of duty worked out in terms of clause (iv) shall apply
to the machinery declared by the units to the Central Excise Department as on
the 1st October, 1991 on single shift basis of 8 working hours:
Provided that the liability of payment of fixed amount of duty shall be
re-assessed by the Board if any of the unit install additional machinery or
equipment.
(2) The units which have short paid the fixed amount of duty during the
financial year 1996-97, the fixed amount of duty less paid during the year
1996-97 shall be worked out in terms of clause (iii) of sub-rule (1) and added
to the liability of payment of fixed amount of duty for the year 1997-98 i
